question.text: With effect from FY 2025-26, the Finance Act 2025 amended Section 2(14) of the ITA. What is the MANAGER-LEVEL implication for a Cat I or Cat II AIF?

answer.text: All AIF income now becomes business income

Securities dealt with by SEBI/IFSCA-registered Cat I and Cat II AIFs are expressly TREATED AS CAPITAL ASSETS; income from their transfer is thus 'capital gains' (not business income) — resolving the long-standing business-income-vs-capital-gains controversy
Cat III AIFs now get pass-through
Listed equity LTCG rate changes to 20%

explanation.text: The Logic: Finance Act 2025 amended Section 2(14) to specifically include securities dealt with by SEBI or IFSCA-registered Cat I and II AIFs within the definition of 'capital asset'. Effect: income from transfer of such securities is taxed as CAPITAL GAINS (concessional rates — 12.5% LTCG/relevant STCG), not as business income at MMR. This resolves the decades-old controversy. Applies from financial year starting 1 April 2025. The Trap: Option A is the opposite of the amendment. Option C — Cat III pass-through is NOT introduced. Option D — listed LTCG rate unchanged at 12.5%. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A covers the amendment at a conceptual level; XIX-C needs to integrate into PPM tax-section updates and investor communications. Manager's Pro-Tip: Update your tax-disclosure section of the PPM post FA 2025 — 'income from transfer of securities by this Cat II AIF will be taxed as capital gains pursuant to the amended Section 2(14) ITA'. LPs have been asking sponsors for this language since FA 2025 was enacted.
